prompt_text: Produce exactly one concise natural‑language caption (a single sentence) that vividly and precisely describes the main subject(s), visible actions and interactions, and the setting; remain concrete, image‑centered and avoid speculation or subjective judgments. For every person or object state whether it is stationary or moving; when describing motion give horizontal direction first then vertical relative to the image frame (for example, "from left to right," "toward the camera while descending"), name the visible phase of motion when apparent (starting/ascending/peaking/descending/landing), indicate whether motions are simultaneous or sequential, and describe each moving subject’s trajectory both relative to the main subject (passing to his right, approaching from behind, moving alongside) and relative to the camera (toward/away from the camera, to the left/right edge of the frame). Specify each person’s head and gaze direction precisely (for example, "looking straight ahead," "eyes down at the phone," "gaze directed up and to the left," or "looking toward the car") to clarify orientation. For interactions with objects or structures state exactly how the subject is using them (holding/gripping/resting/pulling/supporting/leaning on), which hand and side (left/right), and whether the hand is in contact, gripping, merely near, or in motion versus resting. Describe body posture with concrete camera‑relative terms (standing, weight shifted onto left/right leg, slightly leaning forward/back, seated, reclining, crouching, mid‑jump, arms outstretched, knees bent) and specify orientation to the camera (facing the camera, in profile, back to the camera); prefer neutral observable stance descriptors. Clarify precise spatial relationships, counts, arrangement, proximity and scale using camera‑relative language and clear phrases (foreground/midground/background; left/middle/right of frame; across the foreground of; directly in front of/behind; directly overhead; a few feet/meters apart; clustered closely; in a line or scattered). Describe lighting, shadows and visible surface textures with observable cues and an approximate shadow direction or length (for example, "bright direct sunlight casting long shadows toward the lower left," "diffuse overcast," "wet pavement reflecting light"). Report facial expressions or visible affect only when clearly evident using observable detail (open‑mouthed, smiling with teeth visible, furrowed brow). Keep the caption concise, factual and single‑sentence. Output exactly one single sentence.
